- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought signals.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use sentiment as trigger for 3-day smoothing.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 0.5–1% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7), model often misreads momentum; use 14-day EMA of price + sentiment-weighted adjustment (0.3x sentiment) for correction.
